minutes.headline: Parks Commission backed using Board of Health septic money for Marshall Park bathrooms, deferred a decision, and drafted a dog policy.
minutes.summary: The commission discussed a Board of Health offer to fund a septic repair and possibly a bathroom slab at Marshall Park, weighing it against the pending master plan. It reviewed and edited a draft dog policy, which was held for town counsel review and a second read. Updates covered the recreation director search, invasive plants, track resurfacing, Fitzgerald Field custody, and file sharing.

public_comment.topic: No public present; a written comment from a town beach employee about a serious weed problem in the water was read by the chair at t=5839.

votes.outcome: passed 3-0 by roll call (all three present said aye)

budget_items.topic: Board of Health septic repair fund for Marshall Park
budget_items.what_was_said: The Board of Health fund could cover septic design, engineering, installation, piping, and possibly the slab. It would be a grant paid directly to contractors, separate from the town budget.
figures_as_heard: a hundred and five thousand dollars

budget_items.topic: Engineering and design estimate for septic
budget_items.what_was_said: A ballpark engineering and design figure was given, with a plan to ask the Board of Health to release part of the account. This would avoid going out to bid.
Connecting to sewer would mean a district extension, a stub cost, and monthly fees. The Board of Health will not fund sewer connections.
A member floated a later larger restroom with a Title 5 compliant system.
A contractor would likely do herbicide treatment for cost of materials only, with proposal expected in late August.

decisions.decision: Continue discussion of the septic and bathroom proposal, with Dave staying in contact with the Board of Health and members seeking the old parking plan.
Table the dog policy, send it to town manager and town counsel for review, and do a second read at the next meeting.
Add edits: off-leash area begins 50 feet past the Northfield Park sign, leash required in the parking area, 'requires' instead of 'requests', and 'other animals, domestic or wild'.
Next meeting set for August 25 at seven o'clock.
Add Fitzgerald Field and Parameter Burrows property custody transfer to future agendas, aiming for special town meeting.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission took no votes and continued talking about using Board of Health septic money for permanent bathrooms at Marshall Park.
The Board of Health fund could cover septic design and installation, and possibly the slab, as a grant paid to contractors outside the town budget.
The commission tabled the dog policy, sending it to the town manager and town counsel, with a second read planned at the next meeting.
Edits to the draft dog policy set the off-leash area at 50 feet past the Northfield Park sign and required leashes in the parking area.
Fitzgerald Field and Parameter Burrows custody transfer goes on future agendas, aiming for a special town meeting.

why_it_matters: If the Board of Health money pays for the septic work, Marshall Park bathrooms could be built without drawing on the town budget, which is mostly taxes, though the commission has not yet decided.
The dog policy would set leash rules and an off-leash area in town parks, and it has not yet been adopted.
A custody transfer for Fitzgerald Field and Parameter Burrows aimed at a special town meeting could put a vote before residents.
